examples.problem_statement: Consider the equation: $(x-9)(x-5)^3=(x-3)(x-7)^3$. Using the Cross-ADDITION process, we get $4x-24$ on both sides. Verify if the equation satisfies the necessary condition for the Vedic method by checking if $N_1 + D_1 = N_2 + D_2$, where $N_1 = x-9$, $D_1 = x-5$, $N_2 = x-3$, and $D_2 = x-7$.

solution.description: Read the equation (x-9)(x-5)^3 = (x-3)(x-7)^3 and treat it as a candidate for Shunyam Saamyasamuccaye: if both sides produce the same total, that total is zero.

solution.result: \begin{aligned}N_1 = x-9 \\ D_1 = x-5 \\ N_2 = x-3 \\ D_2 = x-7\end{aligned}
solution.description: Name the four binomials: on the left the plain factor N1 = x-9 and the cubed factor D1 = x-5; on the right N2 = x-3 and D2 = x-7. These are the pieces the cross-addition uses.
Because D1 is cubed it counts three times, so form N1 + 3D1 = (x-9) + 3(x-5), which collects to 4x - 24.
Do the same on the right: N2 + 3D2 = (x-3) + 3(x-7) also collects to 4x - 24, the identical total.
The two totals agree, so by the sutra that shared total is zero: 4x - 24 = 0.
Solve the linear equation by adding 24 and dividing by 4, giving x = 6.
Check x = 6 in the original equation: the left side is (-3)(1)^3 = -3 and the right side is (3)(-1)^3 = -3, so both sides match and the answer holds.

concept.technique_name: Samuccaya: common factor equated to zero

solution.description: Start from the equation as given: three fractions that each carry x in the numerator and a sum of two of the letters in the denominator.
Add 3 to both sides so the whole equation reads as an expression equal to zero, the form in which a common factor can be spotted.
Split that 3 into 1 + 1 + 1 so one unit is available to pair with each of the three fractions.
Absorb each 1 into the fraction beside it: (x+a)/(b+c) + 1 becomes (x+a+b+c)/(b+c), and the same happens for the other two, so all three now share the numerator x+a+b+c.
Factor that shared numerator out of all three terms, leaving x+a+b+c multiplied by the sum of the three reciprocals.
A product is zero only when one of its factors is zero, so either x+a+b+c = 0 or the bracket of reciprocals is zero.
The bracket of reciprocals does not vanish here, so the common factor must: x+a+b+c = 0 gives x = -(a+b+c).

concept.technique_name: Merger by a common numerator (Paravartya Yojayet)

examples.problem_statement: Solve the equation: $\frac{x + a^3 + 2b^3}{b - c} + \frac{x + b^3 + 2c^3}{c - a} + \frac{x + c^3 + 2a^3}{a - b} = 2a^2 + 2b^2 + 2c^2 + ab + ac + bc$

solution.description: Look at the shape of the equation: three fractions with the linear denominators b-c, c-a and a-b, and x appearing once in every numerator. That is the merger pattern this method handles.

solution.operation: Let N = x + a^3 + b^3 + c^3
solution.description: Give the repeating part a name: let N = x + a^3 + b^3 + c^3. Every numerator will be rewritten around this single quantity.
Rewrite the first numerator in terms of N. Since N already carries a^3, b^3 and c^3, the numerator x + a^3 + 2b^3 is N + b^3 - c^3.
Split that fraction in two. The second piece is b^3 - c^3 over b - c, which by the difference-of-cubes identity is simply b^2 + bc + c^2, leaving N/(b-c) plus a polynomial.

solution.result: \frac{N}{b-c} + b^2 + bc + c^2 + \frac{N}{c-a} + c^2 + ca + a^2 + \frac{N}{a-b} + a^2 + ab + b^2 = 2a^2 + 2b^2 + 2c^2 + ab + bc + ca
solution.description: Handle the other two fractions the same way, so the left side becomes the three N terms together with b^2+bc+c^2, c^2+ca+a^2 and a^2+ab+b^2.
Collect those three polynomial pieces: they total 2a^2 + 2b^2 + 2c^2 + ab + bc + ca, which is exactly the right-hand side of the original equation.

solution.result: N\left(\frac{1}{b-c} + \frac{1}{c-a} + \frac{1}{a-b}\right) + (2a^2 + 2b^2 + 2c^2 + ab + bc + ca) = 2a^2 + 2b^2 + 2c^2 + ab + bc + ca
solution.description: Write the equation out with the N terms and that collected polynomial on the left and the identical polynomial on the right.
Subtract the matching polynomial from both sides. All that survives is N multiplied by the sum of the three reciprocals, equal to zero.

solution.operation: Note that the sum of reciprocals is not zero
solution.description: Ask whether the reciprocal sum could be the factor that vanishes. For distinct a, b and c it is not zero in general, so it cannot be.
Since the multiplier is not zero, the only way the product can be zero is for N itself to be zero.
